source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Οκτωβρίου — «Αγία Ανθία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους» and «Αγια Ανθια». Its whole notice is one sentence: «Η Αγία Ανθία βρήκε μαρτυρικό θάνατο μέσα σε χάλκινο πυρακτωμένο βόδι» — she found a martyr's death inside a red-hot brazen ox. **An identity question, and it is named in the reader's report.** The corpus keeps `anthia-mother-of-eleutherius` on the Romanian 15 December, whose folder is tied to her son at every line: she was baptised by the Apostle Paul under Hadrian, watched Eleutherius's contest, and was killed embracing his body. Nothing of that is here — no son, no emperor, no Rome — and the manner of death is a different one, so this entry is drafted as a woman of the same name on another day, the way the corpus already carries `domnina-5-january` and `domninus-the-martyr-16-october`. If the writer reads the two as one woman, this folder should be dropped and the Greek row written on the existing one instead. No year, so no `dates`; no place, so no `locations`; no hymn. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
